newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China secured peace pledge from HK gangsters - paper.
newsitem.headline: China secured peace pledge from HK gangsters - paper.

text.p: China secured a pledge from Hong Kong gangsters more than a decade ago not to create chaos in the territory when Britain hands it back to Beijing in June, the Hong Kong Standard newspaper reported on Sunday.
In return, China agreed to turn a blind eye to the activities of crime gangs, known locally as triads,

Quoting former senior Chinese official Wong Man-fong, the newspaper reported the deal was clinched even before December 1984, when China signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration which laid out terms for Hong Kong's return to China at midnight on June 30.
Wong, a former deputy secretary-general of China's official Xinhua News Agency, is now a political commentator.
He was quoted as saying he befriended leaders of Hong Kong's powerful underworld triads.
"I told them that what the administration wanted was a peaceful return and that they could not attempt to do anything to upset Hong Kong's prosperity and stability," Wong said.
"The triad heads basically said they had no intention of causing chaos to Hong Kong's economy since instability meant a drop in their triad business," Wong said.
"But I made the point of warning them that the Communist Party was not someone they wanted to mess with."

Wong was also quoted as saying China's late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping immediately ordered a plan on how to maintain Hong Kong's prosperity after Beijing decided in December 1981 to recover Hong Kong.
Britain wrested Hong Kong from China as war spoils after the opium wars of the 19th century.
